$x$ intercept $(y=0)$

$$\begin{aligned}y&=x^3-12x^2+36x\\0&=x(x^2-12x+36)\\x(x-6)^2&=0\end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=x^3-12x^2+36x\\y'&=3x^2-24x+36\\y''&=6x-24\end{aligned}$$

Stationary points occur when $y'=0$

$$\begin{aligned}3x^2-24x+36&=0\\x^2-8x+12&=0\\(x-2)(x-6)&=0\\ \therefore x&=2\text{ or }x=6\end{aligned}$$

For $x=2$

$$\begin{aligned}y&=2^3-12(2)^2+36(2)\\&=32\\y''&=6(2)-24\\&=-12<0\to\text{conc down}\end{aligned}$$

For $x=6$

$$\begin{aligned}y&=6^3-12(6)^2+36(6)\\&=0\\y''&=6(6)-24\\&=12>0\to\text{conc up}\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Stationary points at $(2,32)$ and $(6,0)$ are a local maximum and a local minimum, respectively.
